title: automobile/inspections
description: One row per ITV roadworthiness inspection of one vehicle. Spanish ITV history. ITV is the compulsory periodic roadworthiness test: a car is first inspected at four years old, then every two years until it turns ten, and annually after that. The inspection dates in this table follow that schedule.

vehicle_id.description: Which car was inspected. Cars under four years old have no rows here at all, because the law does not require a test yet.

inspection_date.description: Date of the test, following the statutory interval for the vehicle's age rather than a random spacing.

result.description: Outcome. 'favourable' passes; 'unfavourable' means defects that must be fixed and retested within two months; 'negative' means the car is unsafe and may not be driven away.

defects.description: What was found, for tests that did not pass outright. Empty on a favourable result, which is about 78% of rows.

mileage_km.description: Odometer reading recorded at the station. ITV centres log this, which is why a car's ITV history is used to detect odometer tampering.

next_due.description: When the next test falls due, computed from the vehicle's age at inspection: two years if under ten, one year if over.

station_code.description: Reference of the testing station. Invented format that does not correspond to the real Spanish station registry.
